name: Factory Records
ownershipStory: Founded in Manchester in 1978 by television presenter Tony Wilson and Alan Erasmus, Factory Records became as well known for its design ethos (every release, and even the label's nightclub, was numbered as a catalogue item) as for its music, and signed Joy Division on a famously artist-friendly contract that gave the band full ownership of their own recordings, unusual for the era. The label went bankrupt in 1992.
hook: A Manchester label that gave its bands complete ownership of their own records, and folded partly because of it.
blurb: Tony Wilson started Factory Records in Manchester in 1978 and ran it on unusually generous contracts that let artists own their work, a direct contrast to the standard major-label contracts behind most of the British labels on this map. It released Joy Division's records. It went bankrupt in 1992, and its end is often told as a warning about how far that generosity could go without a business that could pay for it.
